dimensions.reasons: The submitted renders clearly show a retro-industrial letter-assembly machine: a riveted bench and backplate, left-side gear train, conveyor/rail, two articulated arms, and a final brass word MOMENTUM. Group B frame_0001 through frame_0200 and Group A views show a broadly staged buildup from a mostly empty title area to the completed word.
issues: The mechanism reads as a stylized assembly tableau rather than a clearly legible drive chain suitable for step-by-step teaching.
The supposed letter feed consists largely of featureless rectangular gold blocks and drum-like pieces rather than recognizable scattered 3D letter forms.
The Group C exported-video samples frame_0001 to frame_0016 are visually almost unchanged, so the requested continuous animated sequence is not independently demonstrated by the video frames.

dimensions.reasons: The bench has substantial legs, cross-bracing, a solid plinth, supported rails, and a mounted back panel; the large gear and most structural components appear attached to the machine. The final title letters in Group A momentum_view_0200 visibly stand on the front deck.
issues: Several carried gold blocks and cylindrical pieces appear suspended above the track in Group A momentum_view_0025, momentum_view_0075, and Group B frame_0081, with no consistently readable gripper contact.
The arms have visible pivots but their end effectors are block-like and do not convincingly show how they clamp, flip, or release the workpieces.
The dense left gear/arm/pusher region obscures some mechanical connections, making the physical transmission path difficult to verify.

dimensions.reasons: The final MOMENTUM characters are clearly recognizable as bold, extruded sans-serif letters in the final Group A momentum_view_0200 and Group B frame_0200. The brass/gold letters and gears, cool dark gray steel structure, and brown wood base establish the requested retro-industrial palette.
issues: Most in-process objects on the conveyor are anonymous cuboids, so they do not read as the requested individual letter blanks.
The robotic arms and end effectors are very simplified angular beams and block forms rather than clearly articulated industrial manipulators.
The brass is predominantly clean, uniform gold; visible oxidation and worn variation are limited.

dimensions.reasons: The author-rendered Group B frames are cleanly composed and give the scene believable depth, workshop context, shadows, and substantial manufactured forms. Group B frame_0200 is a coherent finished title-card image with crisp foreground lettering and a controlled blurred industrial background.
issues: Strong motion blur in Group A momentum_view_0075 and Group B frame_0120 makes the arms and carried objects hard to inspect.
Some moving elements look more like floating geometric props than functioning machinery.
The broad background blur hides surrounding workshop detail and reduces the sense of a fully resolved physical environment.

dimensions.reasons: The main spatial hierarchy is sensible: gears and rod hardware occupy the left backplate, a horizontal conveyor spans the middle, arms sit at opposite ends, and the assembled word locks into a front row. This is particularly clear in Group A momentum_view_0200.
issues: The left drive mechanism, pusher, arm, and conveyor overlap heavily, contrary to the target's need for clearly separable teaching layers.
The final oversized foreground letters conceal a significant portion of the conveyor and lower mechanism.
The exact route from gear train through cams/rods to the two arms is not visually traceable.

dimensions.reasons: The gear sizes, arm spans, conveyor height, letter height, and substantial wooden bench read as a consistent single-scale tabletop machine. The large main gear is visibly larger than its driven gears, while the final letters form a balanced title row across the base in Group A momentum_view_0200.
issues: Some foreground letters appear very large relative to the conveyor and working arms, contributing to visual obstruction at the title-card stage.
The blurred oversized background tanks/forms make the overall workshop scale less certain.

dimensions.reasons: Group B frame_0200 shows warm workshop illumination, soft shadows, bright edge highlights on the letters and metal, cool dark-gray steel members, and a matte brown wooden base. Rivets, rail trim, and metallic edges catch light effectively.
issues: Brass weathering/oxidation is subtle; most gold components have a fairly uniform polished appearance.
The steel surfaces are somewhat rough and flat rather than clearly exhibiting the requested clear-coat highlight character.
Motion blur reduces the readability of material detail on moving arms and workpieces in mid-sequence frames.

dimensions.reasons: Visible required components include a large gear with multiple smaller gears, a conveyor-like track, vertical rod/slider hardware, a pusher bar, two articulated arm assemblies, a riveted wood-and-metal bench, and the complete final word MOMENTUM in Group A momentum_view_0200.
issues: Two distinct camshafts driving clearly readable reciprocating push rods are not convincingly visible; only an ambiguous vertical slider/rod arrangement is shown.
The conveyor feed does not visibly carry recognizable letter shapes for most of the sequence.
Correct same-module gear meshing, explicit synchronized drive linkage, and reliable gripping/flipping cannot be confirmed from the shown renders.
The exported Group C video samples do not visibly prove the full pick-and-place progression.

criteria.criterion: The complete machine choreography must assemble and lock MOMENTUM through a synchronized, unobstructed, pedagogically readable sequence.
The complete gear train must satisfy the stated dimensions, common-module compatibility, connected engagement, and mechanically compatible operation.
Two identifiable camshafts must each produce recurring push-rod reciprocation.
The conveyor must have the stated transport length and visibly feed letter blanks into the handling workflow.
Two three-joint robotic arms must both perform letter pick-and-place.
All eight title letters must share the specified bold sans-serif form and dimensions.
The supporting bench must satisfy its dimensions, base role, construction detailing, and complete dark matte wood finish.
The machine must achieve the requested retro-industrial kinetic-typography identity through a coherent old mechanism and its complete brass-and-steel surface system.
criteria.evidence: The completed title and integrated gear-and-arm apparatus clearly form a retro mechanical typography machine in frame_0200, with distinct gold/brass-colored gears and letters, grey metal arms/rails, and a brown wood bench. However, the brass surfaces appear clean, uniformly gold, and glossy/grainy rather than visibly worn or lightly oxidized; no unambiguous patina or oxidation treatment is shown.

criteria.criterion: The native lighting setup and authored result must jointly provide the requested warm key, cool rim, ambient fill, and interior HDRI.
The authored shot must use the requested ordered movement, focal length, and readable shallow-focus treatment.
The delivered Blender project must be openable, editable, complete, and preserve the requested native Cycles rendering configuration and motion-blur result.
The actual PNG sequence and composited MP4 must form a complete, openable output package with the required resolution and timing.

notes: A recognizable, well-rendered retro-industrial kinetic-title machine is present, culminating in a readable MOMENTUM title. The strongest aspects are the finished title-card composition, bench construction, palette, and broad staged progression visible in Group A/B. The main weakness is functional clarity: letter blanks, cams, grippers, supports, and the causal drive chain are too simplified or obscured for the requested teaching-focused mechanical breakdown, while the sampled exported-video frames show no independently visible motion.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
